title: Do Not Take Away Someone's Living

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do not take a pair of millstones—not even the upper one—as security for a debt, because that would be taking a person's livelihood as security. - Deut 24:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Millstones were used daily to grind grain into flour, the very means by which a family made their bread and survived. So God forbids taking a millstone as security for a debt. To do so would be to strip a family of their ability to feed themselves. Even in the legitimate matter of securing a loan, God drew a line, you must not take away the very thing a person needs to live.

This is a striking picture of God's compassion. He cares about the practical survival of the poor and vulnerable. A lender might have a legal right to some security, but not at the cost of a family's daily bread. God's law consistently tilts toward protecting the weak from being crushed by the powerful, even in ordinary financial dealings.

The enduring principle speaks powerfully today. We are not to pursue our own interests, even legitimate ones, in ways that destroy others' ability to survive and thrive. God calls His people to a compassion that considers the real impact of our actions on the vulnerable. This reflects the heart of Christ, who cared deeply for the poor and needy, and who calls us to love our neighbour as ourselves (Jas 2:15-16). Are there ways you can pursue your rights and interests while still guarding the wellbeing of others, especially those with less power than you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you consider how your actions affect the vulnerable?
2. How can you pursue your interests without harming others?
3. Where is God calling you to greater compassion?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a heart of compassion that never crushes the vulnerable. Help me pursue what is right while always guarding others' wellbeing. Amen.
